speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent, and I will be assessing your condition today. To begin, can you describe when the yellowing of your skin and eyes started, and have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior and substance use, have you experienced any recent nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, or abdominal pain? I also need to know if you have had any recent unprotected sexual encounters or shared needles.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see. Given your risk factors, I need to order specific blood work to check for viral hepatitis and liver function. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis Panel, Liver Function Tests, CBC.

speaker: Doctor
text: These lab results indicate severe liver dysfunction with significantly elevated bilirubin and transaminases, along with impaired synthetic function. To distinguish between acute viral hepatitis and other causes like drug-induced liver injury, I need to know: have you experienced any right upper quadrant pain, fever, or joint pains recently?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results show severely impaired liver synthetic function with a prothrombin activity under 40% and an elevated INR, combined with agitation. This clinical picture is consistent with acute liver failure, and given the history, acute viral hepatitis is the leading concern. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Liver Failure
